identity.claim: Tyonek Native Corporation is the ANCSA village corporation for the Native Village of Tyonek, a Dena'ina Athabascan (Tebughna) community on the northwest shore of Cook Inlet.
Headquartered at 880 H Street, Suite 210, Anchorage, AK 99501-5131, phone (907) 272-0707.
Owns and manages more than 200,000 acres of land conveyed under ANCSA in 1971.

Mission, verbatim: 'Tyonek's mission is to profitably manage the Corporation so that Tebughna Shareholders have the opportunity to prosper individually and collectively, as well as with our partners in business'.

Careers page, verbatim: 'Tyonek is an Alaska Native Corporation and our profits support education, health services, and quality-of-life programs for members of the Native Village of Tyonek and our more than 950 shareholders'.
Eight named core values: Tebughna (Land, Tribe, People), Tradition, Pride, Good Health, Trust, Success, Leadership, Knowledge.

size.claim: 2024 gross revenue $341,146,301, ranked No. 21 on Alaska Business Magazine's 2025 Top 49ers.
Employees listed as '1,523 Worldwide | 15 Statewide' in the 2025 Top 49ers listing.
Their own capabilities page states Tyonek 'employs more than 1,300 skilled artisans, technicians, and aviation professionals'.

USASpending lists 22 child recipient registrations under the single parent UEI FM96SF3VF8H9, including near-duplicate entity names registered separately in AK, AL and GA (three separate TFAB Ground Systems registrations, three Tyonek Engineering & Agile Manufacturing registrations).
210,000 square feet of manufacturing, engineering and logistics space across eight buildings in Madison and Huntsville AL and Warner Robins GA.
Workforce composition in their own words: 'more than 50% U.S military veterans, 42% women and 33% minority'.

what_they_do.claim: Capabilities page names the customer set: 'supporting fixed-wing and rotary-wing platforms for all four military services, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and USDA customers'.

Certifications in their own words: 'Our facilities and operations are certified to ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, AS9110, and DCMA 8210.1C standards', plus FAA Part 145 Certified Repair Stations and DCAA/DCMA approved systems.
Stennis facility holds ISO 9001:2015, AS9100 Rev D, AS9110 Rev C, and FAA Part 145 certificate 4SXR048C.

Subsidiaries explicitly listed as SBA-Certified 8(a) on their own site include Tyonek Services Overhaul Facility-Stennis, Tyonek Technical Services, Tyonek Aircraft Overhaul LLC and Tyonek Technical Innovations.

Tyonek Technical Services won FA8773-25-C-0001, a firm-fixed-price level-of-effort 8(a) sole-source award worth $98,115,620 from the Air Force AMIC Detachment 2 at Tinker AFB for Cyber Operations Formal Training Support to the 39th Information Operations Squadron, running through February 28 2027.

Tyonek Aircraft Overhaul LLC won a Coast Guard IDIQ with a $16.8M ceiling and a $3.6M base-year order for replacement voice and flight data recorder units for MH-65E and MH-60T aircraft, announced October 10 2024.
Tyonek Services Group purchased the 68,000 sq ft Huntsville hangar it had leased since 2018, on January 16 2024.

Two FAA-certificated 14 CFR Part 145 Repair Stations, 4SXR048C in Kiln, Mississippi and 7TYR728D in Huntsville, Alabama. NEITHER IS IN ALASKA and neither is at the Madison AL office address. Any Part 145 recordkeeping angle tied to Alaska is a location error.

THE_CENTRAL_PAIN.claim: GAO decision B-424364, B-424364.2, dated June 30 2026. Protester: Tyonek Technical Innovations, LLC, a small business of Anchorage, Alaska. Agency: Department of the Air Force. Solicitation: RFP No. FA8773-25-R-0002 for cyber operations training support services, issued May 19 2025 as an 8(a) small business set-aside under FAR subpart 15.3.

DISPOSITION, and this is load-bearing. 'The protest is dismissed.' GAO did NOT reach the merits and decided NOTHING about the quality of Tyonek's past performance. Ground one, untimeliness: the challenge was to the solicitation's terms and had to be raised before the proposal due date, because 'the plain language of the solicitation made it unambiguously clear how the agency intended to treat the past performance information of affiliated companies.' Ground two, prematurity: the challenge 'essentially challenges the agency's evaluation judgments before the award decision has been made.' Tyonek REMAINED IN THE COMPETITION and no award had been made.

The solicitation's affiliate past-performance rule, quoted as the full contiguous block rather than its last sentence alone, because the first three sentences carry the qualifier that affiliate performance IS considered when documented: 'Affiliate companies, sister companies, teaming arrangements, joint venture agreement, etc., will be considered, provided that sufficient documentation is included in the proposal. The prime contractor must demonstrate that the affiliate will perform significant and critical aspects of the contract if awarded. Proposal documentation should include a copy of the signed arrangement such as documented affiliation, a copy of the teaming agreement, a copy of the joint venture agreement, etc. If the required information is not included in the proposal, the proposed affiliate companies, sister companies, joint venture companies, etc. shall not be evaluated or considered.'

NEEDS RE-VERIFICATION, URL supplied this round. Mechanical Quality Inspector II posting, Madison AL, lists among duties 'Complete non-conformance reports as required' and 'Complete AS9102 FAI reports'. If the posting no longer resolves, REJECT rather than assume.

NEEDS RE-VERIFICATION, URL supplied this round. industry_grounding.claim: FAA estimate, quoted exactly as written and scoped as written: 'estimates the total annual burden on the international repair station community to be 240,869 hours costing $11,507,548 annually.' THIS IS AN INDUSTRY-WIDE ANNUAL TOTAL for the repair station community. It is NOT a per-company figure and NOT Tyonek's burden, and it must never be placed next to Tyonek's two repair stations in a way that implies their scale. The scope of 'the international repair station community' is not resolvable from the page, so the phrase must be quoted as written and never silently rendered as 'all US repair stations'.

CORRECTED FRAMING, previously stated wrongly. ARSA's words: 'Considering all recordkeeping requirements and not just completion of an application on FAA From 8310-3 resulted in a 23,000 percent increase in hours and a 2,600 percent increase in estimated cost.' This is a change in the FAA's OWN ESTIMATING METHODOLOGY between two Federal Register notices, from counting only Form 8310-3 completion to counting all part 145 recordkeeping. The burden on operators did NOT rise 23,000 percent, the measurement scope did. It is also ARSA's characterization, not the FAA's. Any sentence implying an exploding compliance burden is FALSE and may not ship.

14 CFR 145.213(d): 'only an employee appropriately certificated as a mechanic or repairman under part 65 is authorized to sign off on final inspections and maintenance releases for the repair station.'
14 CFR 43.9 states that the approving person's signature 'constitutes the approval for return to service.'

22 CFR 120.54(b)(1) requires, for the ITAR end-to-end encryption carve-out, that 'the data is not in an unencrypted form' between originator and intended recipient and that 'the means of decryption are not provided to any third party.'

DFARS 252.204-7012 requires that any external cloud service used to store, process or transmit covered defense information meet security requirements equivalent to the FedRAMP Moderate baseline, and flows down to subcontractors.

GAO found the military services 'generally lack metrics to evaluate the results of predictive maintenance', that improvement examples come 'from limited experience', and that the services 'do not replace parts or components regularly based on predictive maintenance forecasts'.

The DoD Office of Inspector General found the Pentagon has not fully implemented predictive maintenance on any existing weapon system, with officials naming lack of quality data and lack of data-analyst skillsets as primary blockers.

Oliver Wyman's MRO Survey of over 150 aviation professionals found 58 percent said their companies were stuck at the 'experimental' stage of AI in both 2025 and 2026, with data infrastructure the named obstacle.

GAO on the F-35 ALIS: critical data 'often inaccurate or missing', forcing maintainers to track information manually in Excel; corrupt or missing electronic records caused ALIS to signal an aircraft should not fly when maintainers knew it was safe.

McKinsey states that in aircraft maintenance 'gen AI platforms won't be flawless, and thus airlines and MRO providers should not blindly rely on them in critical scenarios' and that 'humans are always in the driver's seat'.
EASA's AI Concept Paper Issue 2 provides usable guidance only for Level 1 AI (human assistance) and Level 2 AI (human-AI teaming under human oversight). Level 3 advanced automation is not addressed.

competitive_field.claim: Tyonek's own capabilities page lists CNC machining, welding, coatings, CMM and laser scan inspection, reverse engineering, manufacturing space, aircraft bays, FAA Part 145 stations and cyber training, and contains no mention of AI, machine learning, predictive maintenance, automation or data analytics.

Yulista Holding, an Alaska Native Corporation aerospace and defense holding company in Huntsville, publishes a named AI service portfolio including 'AI Infrastructure Design & Deployment', 'Local and Cloud Model Hosting' and 'End-User Enablement and AI Adoption'. It is sold as an IT service line to government customers, and nothing on the page claims AI applied inside Yulista's own MRO operations.
Yulista Support Services was awarded a potential $219.4M five-year Army IDIQ in July 2024 for aviation modernization and maintenance support, as a total 8(a) small business set-aside.

Amentum states on its Army aviation capability page: 'To improve quality and cost effectiveness, Amentum has introduced technological innovations including augmented reality and artificial intelligence.'

V2X markets AMMO (Aircraft Maintenance and Management Optimization), described as a real-time integrated platform, and states it 'operationalizes massive volumes of maintenance and logistics data using advanced data analytics' on 'a secure, AI-ready cloud foundation'.

Akima's aviation capability page names no AI, no analytics, no predictive maintenance and no automation, while its separate Akima Emerging Technologies operating company markets AI, machine learning and robotic process automation.

M1 Support Services, a mid-size non-ANC competitor with 5,000+ employees and 570+ aircraft platforms, publishes no AI, machine learning, predictive maintenance or analytics language on its corporate site.

Chugach Government Solutions' corporate site technology language stops at IT Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Enterprise IT & Sustainment and System Integration, with no mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation or analytics.

values_screen.ice_immigration: CLEAR. Independent USASpending screening of the top 100 awards found zero ICE awards: 89 Department of Defense, 5 U.S. Customs and Border Protection, 2 GSA, 2 SOCOM, 1 DTRA, 1 Coast Guard. The five CBP rows are Tyonek Aircraft Overhaul radar and aerostat sustainment (TARS sites, maritime approaches surveillance towers, a radar purchase). Their own customer list names CBP but not ICE. The Alaska Public Media investigation of ANCs in ICE detention does not mention Tyonek.
values_screen.fca_qui_tam: NOTHING FOUND. The same search surfaced a DOJ FCA resolution involving a different ANC subsidiary pair, so the search was capable of surfacing this class of result.
values_screen.labor: One routine NLRB representation election, Case 20-RC-321767, Mather CA, IAM District Lodge 725 certified September 27 2023. Case closed. Not adverse.
values_screen.environmental: Tyonek appears as a RECIPIENT of EPA assistance under the Contaminated ANCSA Lands Assistance Program, not as a violator.
values_screen.employee_sentiment: 3.5 of 5 across 164 Indeed reviews, normal spread for a 1,500-person multi-site contractor, with both harsh and positive reviews present. Not a disqualifier and not to be dressed up.
values_screen.verdict: No values conflict found that would embarrass an honesty-first brand. The CBP line is noted honestly and is aviation and sensor sustainment, not detention or enforcement operations.

known_conflicts_for_factchecker: Land acreage: 'more than 200,000 acres' on tyonek.com vs 'more than 190,000 acres' in the Top 49ers listing.
Shareholder count: 'roughly 938' (2019), 'more than 950' (careers page), 'over 1,000' (Oct 2024 press release).
Employee count: '1,523 Worldwide' (Top 49ers) vs 'more than 1,300' (their capabilities page) vs 'Fewer than 500' (SAM small-business size representation) vs ~744 (LinkedIn).
A '$13.8 million annual revenue' figure from an aggregator snippet is flatly inconsistent with the Top 49ers $341M and must not be used.

fact_checker_round_1.drift_pattern_found: PAIN INFLATION. Three substantive rejections all leaned the same way, toward making Tyonek look more troubled and more regulatorily squeezed than the sources support. The GAO item turned a procedural dismissal in which Tyonek stayed in the competition into the appearance of an adverse past-performance ruling. The 23,000 percent item turned a change in FAA counting method into an exploding burden. The 240,869 hour item put an industry-wide total where a reader reads it as Tyonek's load. Individually small, together a narrative the pages do not support, and one the prospect can disprove by clicking a link, because her own employer is the protester in that decision.
fact_checker_round_1.showrunner_response: All three corrected above rather than softened. The honest finding is not that Tyonek is drowning. It is that Tyonek is a procedurally sophisticated operator that litigates its proposal terms at GAO, running a genuine multi-standard recordkeeping surface across a many-entity structure. Sell to that.
